kicker: Google's TabFM, read from its code

scenes.headline: How TabFM reads a table it has never seen
scenes.sub: Google's zero-shot tabular model, read from its code.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Scribble! TabFM is Google's zero-shot model for spreadsheets. Here's how it works, read from its code.

scenes.text: TabFM needs no column vocabulary. A column is just a position, and the only thing it knows about your schema is the column count.
scenes.mark: A column is just a position
scenes.say: TabFM needs no column vocabulary. A column is just a position; all it knows about your schema is how many columns there are.

steps.note: offsets 0, 1 and 3, wrapping past the last column
steps.say: A wrapper first turns the table into plain floats. Then each cell is grouped with the cells one and three columns to its right, and Fourier-expanded.
Column attention and row attention alternate, twice each. Rows carry no order; columns get rotary positions.
Eight CLS tokens per row are concatenated into one vector, two thousand and forty-eight wide. The cell grid is thrown away.

steps.note: a key-side mask: queries never see each other
steps.say: A twenty-four block transformer, ninety-eight point eight percent of the weights, reads those rows. Each row attends only to the labelled context rows.
One catch: column order matters, so the default runs thirty-two passes, each with shuffled columns, and averages them.

scenes.title: Where the zero-shot skill comes from

left.title: A gradient-boosted tree
items: Re-derives the structure from your data, every time
left.say: A gradient-boosted tree needs no shared input space. It re-derives the structure from your data, every time.

right.title: TabFM's synthetic prior
items: Hundreds of millions of synthetic datasets
right.say: TabFM trained on hundreds of millions of synthetic tables from causal models, so a new table's structure looks familiar.

scenes.title: TabArena classification Elo, live board
scenes.say: On the live board, TabFM sits three hundred and forty Elo above the best tuned tree. Four newer models now sit above it.

scenes.text: Keep the table-reading front end tiny, and spend the depth on in-context learning over compressed rows.

recap: A column is a position; only the count is known
Cells compress to one 2048-wide vector per row
Pretrained only on synthetic causal-model tables
scenes.say: To recap: no column vocabulary, one vector per row, and a synthetic prior.
